//: Who may touch what, written down BEFORE anyone starts. Read docs/parallel-dev.md first, then BOTH briefs: docs/specs/unipile-rooms-and-booking.md and docs/specs/adgrant-and-dev-agents.md. THIS IS PROGRAMME THREE, second half. Its first five parcels are landed and are kept in docs/parcels-programme-3-landed.json; programme two's thirteen are in docs/parcels-programme-2.json and programme one's nineteen in docs/parcels-programme-1.json. None of those three files is for running. Ownership freed by a retired parcel is reused here on purpose: adgrant-site inherits the AdGrant tree from adgrant-front, and booking-picker inherits the dialog from booking-dialog.
//brief: Two briefs, and a parcel reads the one its prompt names. unipile-rooms-and-booking.md carries the Unipile contract, the identity decisions and the rule that every inbound message is checked for who it is from, who it is to and which chat it is in. adgrant-and-dev-agents.md carries adgrant.ai's own content API, the six factual defects in the material being carried over, the split between generating a structure and uploading it, and the answer to the owner's question about per-agent limits. An agent that starts from a paraphrase instead will rebuild something that already exists or ship something that is wrong.
//seams: Files everything needs. A parcel may ADD up to three lines to one of these and delete none, and must declare which lines up front. Two one-line additions merge by keeping both; two thirty-line edits merge into something nobody can verify. THREE STATED EXCEPTIONS, carried over because the three-line grammar would make them unusable: scripts/build-kb.ts admits one appended Corpus const plus its name on the CORPORA line, shared/roster.ts admits one whole appended agent entry, and client/src/components/site/doors/bodies.tsx admits one door-to-body entry. All three are appends at the end of a list, which is the shape that merges. A FOURTH, added for programme three: shared/schema.ts admits one re-export line. A new table is fifteen lines and the seam allows three, so a parcel that needs a table writes it in its OWN file and re-exports it from the schema - drizzle-kit follows the export, and one line merges where fifteen do not.
//frozen: Nobody edits these during a parallel run. A change here invalidates every parcel at once. Programme three has one consequence worth stating: client/index.html carries the one <head> this application serves, so a second site on a second host cannot have its own title and meta without editing a frozen file. That is why adgrant-front builds a route tree and not a second host - the host switch is owner work, done when no wave is running.
//alone: Parcels marked runAlone touch the room, the panel or the shell - everything reads those, and two agents in them at once produce a merge nobody can check. One agent, let it finish, then start the others.
//order: The waves are in scripts/build-prompts.mjs and check-parcels.mjs reads them back. Programme three's ordering is a dependency chain, not a preference, and it has three links. (1) unipile-core is wave one ALONE because four parcels import its client; a parcel that writes its own Unipile client because the shared one did not exist yet is four incompatible error mappers. (2) booking-server and booking-dialog are the same wave and build to the request and response shapes fixed in the brief's section 3 - that is what fixing them in writing was for. (3) room-identity precedes login-create-room, because the claim dialog the site's new menu opens is the one room-identity builds. Beyond the chain, one standing rule: AT MOST ONE PARCEL PER WAVE MAY TOUCH server/routes.ts. Three parcels here need a route, and they are in three different waves for that reason alone.

server/routes.ts: the two routes that connect and drop a visitor's calendar
shared/api.ts: what the picker learns about a connected calendar

visitor-calendar.why: The owner has asked for this four times and it has never existed. It was designed, he published a Google Cloud app for it with the non-sensitive calendar.freebusy scope, and then no parcel ever built it — while /privacy described it in the present tense until that was found and corrected. It is also what blocks the demo video Google's verification wants, because there is no flow to record.
visitor-calendar.done: A VISITOR CAN CONNECT THEIR OWN GOOGLE CALENDAR SO WE DO NOT OFFER THEM A TIME THEY ARE ALREADY BUSY. Read docs/review/next-waves.md, section visitor-calendar, first. THE CREDENTIALS ARE SET on the deployment as GOOGLE_FREEBUSY_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_FREEBUSY_CLIENT_SECRET — the owner's own Google Cloud app, separate from the scheduling connector's, which is OURS and stays. Read them from there, document both in .env.example, and BE COMPLETELY INERT WITHOUT THEM: a fork has no such app, so the picker there shows no such option and says nothing about one. WHY NOT THROUGH THE SCHEDULING CONNECTOR, which already holds the owner's own calendar and would seem to save a whole integration: because the connector has NO FREE/BUSY ENDPOINT — the brief records that — so availability there is computed by LISTING EVENTS, and a visitor connecting through it would be handing over event titles, guests and locations to answer a question whose whole content is 'busy or not'. Direct is not the long way round, it is the narrow one: freeBusy.query returns intervals and nothing else, which is why the scope is non-sensitive and why the consent screen is light rather than a Google security review. It is also the only shape in which the connection can be temporary — a token held for the length of the pick and never written down — where a connector account is a row in a tenant that persists until somebody deletes it. (1) ASK FOR calendar.freebusy AND NOTHING ELSE at authorize time. The owner's app currently has four non-sensitive scopes registered on it — calendar.freebusy, calendar.events.freebusy, calendar.calendarlist.readonly and calendar.events.public.readonly. Registering a scope is not requesting it, and this asks for one; say in the code WHY, and tell the owner he can delete the two nobody requests so the consent screen lists only what is used. It is non-sensitive precisely because freeBusy.query returns busy intervals — no titles, no guests, no locations, no descriptions — and asking for one field more turns a light consent screen into a Google security review. (2) IT IS THE VISITOR'S GOOGLE, NOT OURS. Two apps, two consent screens. The visitor's token is held for the length of the booking and never written down: not to the database, not to a log, not to a session store that outlives the pick. The connection ends when they confirm or after five minutes, whichever comes first. (3) DISCONNECTING REMOVES THAT VISITOR'S OWN GOOGLE ACCOUNT AND NOTHING ELSE — never dan@top-rated.team, never any LinkedIn or WhatsApp account. The owner said so in those words. (4) BUSY MEANS OFFERED-AS-BUSY, NOT HIDDEN: a slot the visitor is busy in is marked, not removed, because a person may still choose it, and silently shrinking the list makes the picker look broken. (5) THE PRIVACY PAGE MOVES BACK TO THE PRESENT TENSE IN THE SAME COMMIT, not before and not after. Its row currently says, correctly, that this is not built; that row is part of this parcel and it is the last thing to change. (6) A FORK HAS NO SUCH APP, so this is off there by default and the picker never mentions it. WHAT MUST NOT CHANGE: our own calendar is still read through the scheduling connector, and the slot list is still computed the way server/booking/slots.ts computes it today — this ADDS a second, optional overlay from the visitor's side, it does not replace the first.

upwork-promo-video.why: The owner asked for a promo animation for the Top-Rated Team page on Upwork and it was never made. Nothing about it exists in this repository — no file, no reference — and I let that sit rather than saying so, which is the part worth not repeating.
upwork-promo-video.done: TWO SHORT PROMO ANIMATIONS, RENDERED BY A SCRIPT, NOT BY HAND. One in this site's own visual language, one in Upwork's; the owner asked for both so he can see which lands. THE METHOD IS THE POINT: `npx tsx scripts/build-promo-video.ts` drives headless Chrome over an HTML timeline, captures frames through CDP Page.startScreencast, and pipes them to ffmpeg — both are already on this machine, so this is a script that runs rather than a plan. A hand-edited video goes stale the day a price or a service name changes and nobody notices; one built from shared/doors.ts, shared/pricing.ts and shared/adgrant.ts cannot say a number the site does not. READ THE REAL SOURCES: the door headlines, the price rows and the measured figures come from those modules, and the promo must not state a claim that is not already true on the site — the same rule the rest of this repository is written to. WHAT UPWORK ACTUALLY ACCEPTS is the first thing to check and to write down in the script's header: the aspect ratio, the maximum length and the file size the profile page takes, from Upwork's own documentation, with the URL. Guessing that and rendering ninety seconds of 4K is a wasted wave. KEEP IT SHORT. Under sixty seconds, no voice-over, legible with the sound off, and readable as a thumbnail — a profile video is watched muted in a list. NO CLAIM THAT NEEDS A LAWYER: no result promised, no client named without permission, and no logo of a company we do not have the right to show. Output to docs/promo/, and print the duration, the dimensions and the byte size at the end so the owner can check it against Upwork's limits without opening it.

case-studies-doc.why: The PDF is the thing that gets sent to a buyer and its title says only 'Case Studies', which tells that buyer nothing about what this company does. The owner wants the niche in the title, the year and his name in the filename, and — the harder half — an editable copy he can correct text and photographs in, with the corrections not lost the next time the file is generated.
case-studies-doc.done: THE TITLE, THE FILENAME, AND AN HONEST ANSWER ABOUT THE EDITABLE COPY. (1) THE TITLE becomes 'Case Studies: Google Ads and Paid Ads, Organic LinkedIn growth and any AI agents or custom development' — the owner's own words, verbatim. (2) THE FILENAME becomes '{current year} Dan Burykin & his Top-Rated Team case studies.pdf', with the year read from the clock at build time and not typed. Update the npm script so `npm run cases:pdf` writes that name. (3) THE EDITABLE COPY. The owner wants a Google Doc he can change text and images in, staying in step with the site and with edits made here. DO NOT PRETEND THAT IS A ONE-WAY EXPORT. Establish and WRITE DOWN in the script's header which direction is authoritative, because both cannot be: today shared/cases.ts is generated from the repository and the PDF is generated from it, so a Google Doc edited by hand is a third copy that the next build silently overwrites. The honest shapes are (a) export only — the Doc is a snapshot, clearly dated, and edits there are lost, or (b) the Doc becomes the source for the prose and the build reads it back, which needs Drive access this deployment does not have. PICK ONE, say which, and build it; do not build a two-way sync that quietly loses somebody's afternoon. A .docx that Google Docs imports without mangling the layout is a reasonable (a): produce it beside the PDF from the same HTML. (4) NOTHING IN THE PDF MAY BECOME UNTRUE: the cases, the figures and the screenshots come from shared/cases.ts and the repository's own captures, and the title change must not turn a portfolio into a claim about results.

shared/doors.ts: whatever a second in-house catalogue needs, added

adgrant-as-fork.why: AdGrant.AI is a second product hand-built inside this repository, and the owner's point is that it should have been the first in-house FORK of it — the same doors, rooms, agents and sign-in, re-pointed at what each service means for a nonprofit. Doing it now is worth more than the tidiness: it is the only honest test of the fork path before a real partner uses it, and there is already a white-label request against adgrant.ai itself, which means a fork OF a fork has to work.
adgrant-as-fork.done: ADGRANT.AI IS A CATALOGUE, NOT A HAND-BUILT SECOND SITE. Read shared/catalogue.ts and shared/operator.ts first — the fork machinery already exists and has tests; this parcel makes our own second product use it instead of going around it. (1) EVERY SERVICE IS CLONED, including the ones hidden for the LinkedIn review, with its page, its room, its members and its agent — and every name, headline, blurb, starter and agent prompt re-pointed at what that service does FOR A NONPROFIT. A cloned row that still says what the Top-Rated Team row says is worse than no row: it tells a nonprofit we sell something we do not. (2) ALL THREE WAYS IN WORK THERE, and the design and the chrome stay AdGrant.AI's own — an in-house fork keeps its face. (3) A FORK OF A FORK MUST WORK. There is a live white-label request against adgrant.ai. Establish what happens when a partner forks a deployment that is itself a fork: whose legal name, whose terms, whose contact, whose agents, and what the room footer says. Write it into docs/specs/forking.md with the answer for each, and make the catalogue resolver do it rather than leaving it to be discovered. (4) NOTHING THE OWNER ALREADY HAS MAY REGRESS: the 27 library pages, the generator, the templates, the head rewrite per host, the sitemap, the redirects from /adgrant. There are tests for most of that — run them, do not re-derive them. (5) ITS OWN PRIVACY AND TERMS, at its own addresses, and the footer links move to them in the same commit that creates them — they point at Top-Rated Team's today, which is honest and wrong. A fork gets them part-filled from what it actually has: its login methods, its rooms, and any partner services added. (6) THE FRONT PAGE OPENS THE SAME WAY OURS DOES. The hero carries the Sign in | Open a room pair, and the door itself carries a chat with the Ad Grant agent — a nonprofit should be able to ask a question on the page it landed on, not after finding a room. Both already exist on top-rated.team (client/src/components/site/RoomMenu.tsx and the door bodies); reuse them through the catalogue rather than building a second pair with the same words on it. WHAT MUST NOT CHANGE: adgrant.ai keeps answering at the root with its own head, icon and card, and top-rated.team/adgrant keeps 301ing to it.

server/routes.ts: the route that hands a template's files over, behind a sign-in
shared/api.ts: what the page learns about the files it may have

adgrant-room-setup.why: A template page hands over exactly two files — one Editor CSV and one list of callouts and snippets — while the page above it counts seven kinds of thing. The owner wants each of those counts to be a file, wants the files behind a sign-in rather than free to anyone, and reports that 'Build the files again' does nothing when pressed.
adgrant-room-setup.done: EVERY COUNT ON THE PAGE IS A FILE, AND THE FILES ARE WORTH SIGNING IN FOR. (1) ONE CSV PER ENTITY, beside the single Editor file that already exists: campaigns, ad groups, keywords, ads, sitelinks, callouts, structured snippets. The seven numbers listed on the page become seven links, and a number with no link beside it is a number that should not be listed. Each file must import on its own; say in the page which tool takes which. (2) BEHIND A SIGN-IN — the same three ways as top-rated.team, and Resend is already configured for this domain so the email way works. State plainly on the page, BEFORE the sign-in, what it is for: the files are free, the account is so the work can continue in a room. Do not invent a new sign-in; use the one this deployment has. (3) 'BUILD THE FILES AGAIN' DOES NOTHING and the owner pressed it. Either it rebuilds and says so, or it is not a button. Decide, and make the label true. (4) THE REAL PLACE FOR THIS IS A ROOM. Once somebody is signed in, downloading the files and uploading the setup through the official Google Ads API both belong in their room, with the agent, not on a public page — that is the owner's standing design and the page should lead there rather than being the destination. (5) NEW ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES, if any, go in .env.example with one line each saying what breaks without them; the owner asked what to add, so the answer must be readable there rather than in a commit message. NOTHING IS WRITTEN INTO ANYBODY'S GOOGLE ADS ACCOUNT by this parcel, and every campaign in every file is still Paused.

server/routes.ts: the admin routes, behind the owner's own sign-in
shared/api.ts: what a row in the admin list looks like

people-admin.why: There is no way to see who has used this. The owner wants one plain page: the people who have signed in, by which method, with whatever contact detail that method legitimately gave us, their rooms, their activity, their bookings, and whether they are a white-label partner.
people-admin.done: ONE PAGE, AND IT IS ONLY EVER READ BY THE PERSON WHO RUNS THE DEPLOYMENT. (1) AUTHORISATION FIRST AND IT IS THE WHOLE PARCEL. This page lists people, their contact details and links into their rooms — a room address is a bearer credential, so this is the most dangerous page in the repository. It is reachable only by the operator of THIS deployment, proved by the session from room-account, and there is no other way in: no shared password, no secret path, no 'unlisted' URL. Write that test before the page. (2) WHAT IT SHOWS: each person, which ways they signed in with, the contact detail each of those ways legitimately yielded and nothing beyond it, their rooms with links, when each was last active, their bookings and whether each still stands, and their white-label partner status. Later, orders and tasks per room — leave the shape room for it, build none of it. (3) IT SHOWS WHAT WE HAVE, NOT WHAT WOULD BE USEFUL. A WhatsApp sign-in gives a peppered chat hash and a display name, not a phone number, and the page must say the phone is not held rather than leave a blank that reads like missing data. (4) IT FORKS, EMPTY. A partner's deployment gets this page with their own people and no trace of ours — the same catalogue rules as everything else — and with only the contact fields their own sign-in methods produce. (5) READ-ONLY in this parcel. No deleting a person, no cancelling somebody's booking from here: every one of those is an action with consequences elsewhere and each deserves its own thinking.

testimonials.why: Neither site carries a word from anybody who has worked with this team, and the owner wants one on each — specific and numerate rather than warm and vague.
testimonials.done: A TESTIMONIALS SECTION ON BOTH SITES, AND NOT ONE INVENTED WORD. THIS IS THE RULE THAT DECIDES THE PARCEL: every quotation is either something a real person actually said, with their permission, or it is not published. This repository has already had to grow a guard in scripts/build-adgrant.ts because a vague claim was turned into a precise false one, and a fabricated client quotation is the same failure with a name attached to it. SO: build the SECTION — the component, the shape, the layout, the place on each page — and fill it from shared/testimonials.ts, which starts with whatever real material exists. Look first: the Upwork agency profile at upwork.com/agencies/google carries public reviews, and docs/case-studies.html and shared/cases.ts carry measured outcomes. Where a quotation cannot be sourced, leave the row out and render the section with what there is; if there is nothing, the section does not appear at all and the page is unchanged. WHAT THE OWNER ASKED FOR IN THE COPY AROUND IT, which is ours to write and can therefore be written now: that this is digital expertise blended with subject-matter AI agents and any agents a client brings, working on Google Ads, paid advertising, organic LinkedIn growth and custom development — with the numbers this repository already measures rather than new ones. NOTE the LinkedIn services are hidden for the API review, so the LinkedIn clause follows shared/linkedin-review.ts like every other mention.
